name: MI-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about nine points on partisan fundamentals
Jeremy Moss holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage over Ethan Baker, plus outside support
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 95 percent
Open seat with no polling or expert ratings, adding some uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's Democratic lean, Moss's dominant fundraising edge, and markets pricing this near 95 percent for Democrats all point to a comfortable hold despite Stevens's retirement. The open-seat status and absence of polling justify only a modest trim from the fundamentals-based expectation.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or a strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would require a much larger shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Haley Stevens (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Haley Stevens's run for U.S. Senate leaves this Detroit-area seat open, but the district's nine-point Democratic lean gives the party a strong structural advantage. State Senator Jeremy Moss enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised about 1.5 million dollars to Ethan Baker's roughly 142,000, and outside groups have added nearly 300,000 dollars on his side. Baker has kept pace in neither fundraising nor outside support.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, money, and market pricing, all of which point the same way. An independent candidate has raised a notable sum but is unlikely to alter the two-party outcome. The seat remains firmly in the Democratic column.
